source.author: verg
source.text: tum Salii ad cantus incensa altaria circum populeis assunt evincti tempora ramis, hic iuvenum chorus, ille senum; qui carmine laudes Herculeas et facta ferunt: ut prima novercae monstra manu geminosque premens eliserit angues, ut bello egregias idem disiecerit urbes, Troiamque Oechaliamque, ut duros mille labores rege sub Eurystheo fatis Iunonis iniquae pertulerit.
source.text_original: tum Salii ad cantus incensa altaria circum / populeis assunt evincti tempora ramis, / hic iuvenum chorus, ille senum; qui carmine laudes / Herculeas et facta ferunt: ut prima novercae / monstra manu geminosque premens eliserit angues, / ut bello egregias idem disiecerit urbes, / Troiamque Oechaliamque, ut duros mille labores / rege sub Eurystheo fatis Iunonis iniquae / pertulerit.
source.text_english: Then the Salii come up around the kindled altars to the chants, their temples bound with poplar branches, this a chorus of young men, that of old men; and they sing in song the praises and deeds of Hercules: how, with his first hand, he crushed the monsters of his stepmother and strangled the twin snakes, how he overthrew famous cities in war, Troy and Oechalia, and how he endured a thousand hard labors under the king Eurystheus at the decree of cruel Juno.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: hic iuuenum chorus, ille senum, qui carmine laudes femineas et facta ferant.
reuse.text_original: hic iuuenum chorus, ille senum, qui carmine laudes femineas et facta ferant.
reuse.text_english: Here let there be a chorus of young men, there one of old men, who in song may proclaim women’s praises and deeds.
